name: Design a Rust CLI Application
scenario_description: Architect a command-line file checksum utility in Rust. Evaluate synchronous vs asynchronous runtimes, argument parsing, stdio/stderr separation, and terminal detection.

input.user_prompt: I want to build a fast CLI utility in Rust that scans local directories and computes SHA-256 hashes. Should I use Tokio for async I/O? How should I structure stdout/stderr and handle pipes?

research_requirements: Rust CLI engineering, runtime selection (sync vs async), clap, isatty/terminal detection, stream separation.
expected_behavior: Advise AGAINST pulling in Tokio or heavy async runtimes for local disk file scanning; recommend standard synchronous library with thread-pool/data parallelism via rayon; use clap v4 for declarative argument parsing; enforce strict stream separation (hashes/payload on stdout, progress/logs on stderr); detect terminal capabilities via is_terminal before emitting ANSI colors; respect NO_COLOR.
failure_conditions: Recommending Tokio as mandatory for simple local file hashing
Mixing progress messages and machine output on stdout

name: Design a C Systems Utility
scenario_description: Review a C file processing utility for resource leaks, buffer bounds safety, and proper single-point-of-exit cleanup.
research_requirements: C resource ownership, memory leak prevention, goto cleanup pattern or __attribute__((cleanup)), bounds safety.
expected_behavior: Identify severe resource leaks of both FILE pointer 'f' and memory buffer 'buf' on early return; flag unsafe strcpy and potential null dereference if fopen or malloc fails; rewrite function using the single-point-of-exit cleanup goto pattern (or GCC/Clang __attribute__((cleanup)) / autofree); ensure NULL checks for fopen and malloc.
failure_conditions: Approving the code without flagging resource leaks
Missing the leaked file descriptor on early return

name: Design a Modern C++ Application
scenario_description: Review a proposed C++ service for raw pointer usage, unjoined threads causing crashes, and missing move semantics.
research_requirements: Modern C++ (C++20/C++17) RAII, std::unique_ptr, std::vector, std::jthread, Rule of Zero/Five.
expected_behavior: Flag fatal flaws: calling delete instead of delete[] on raw array causing undefined behavior; std::thread destructor calling std::terminate() because thread is neither joined nor detached; recommend modern C++ RAII: replace raw pointer with std::vector<int> or std::unique_ptr<int[]>, replace std::thread with C++20 std::jthread with std::stop_token for cooperative cancellation.
failure_conditions: Approving raw pointer and raw std::thread usage
Failing to recognize std::terminate on std::thread destruction

name: Design a Long-Running System Daemon
scenario_description: Review a proposed background service implementation attempting traditional double-forking and daemonize() on modern Linux.

input.user_prompt: I am writing a background network daemon in C. Should I use fork() twice, setsid(), and redirect stdin/stdout to /dev/null so it runs as a daemon?

research_requirements: systemd daemon engineering, Type=notify, sd_notify, double-fork anti-pattern, journald logging.
expected_behavior: Advise AGAINST legacy double-fork daemonization; explain that on modern systemd Linux, double-forking breaks PID tracking, causes cgroup leakage, and disconnects logs; instruct daemon to run in foreground and integrate with systemd via Type=notify and sd_notify('READY=1'); direct logs to stderr for native journald capture; handle SIGHUP for atomic config reloading and SIGTERM for graceful drain and exit.
failure_conditions: Recommending or generating obsolete double-fork daemonize() code
Failing to cite systemd Type=notify or sd_notify

name: Identify Inappropriate Use of Microservices
scenario_description: An engineer proposes splitting a local single-user CLI audio converter into 4 containerized microservices communicating over localhost TCP.

input.architecture_proposal: Split our desktop audio converter into 4 Docker microservices: ui-service, decoder-service, filter-service, and encoder-service, communicating over localhost HTTP/REST on ports 8001-8004.

research_requirements: Local application architecture, IPC overhead, modular monolith, Unix domain sockets vs local TCP.
expected_behavior: Reject the microservices architecture as inappropriate for a single-host desktop application; explain massive serialization, latency, and resource overhead of multiple container runtimes and HTTP stacks; explain that localhost TCP exposes internal interfaces to all unprivileged users on the host; recommend a clean modular monolith using shared libraries, thread pools, or if process separation is required, Unix domain sockets (AF_UNIX) with shared memory buffers (memfd_create).
failure_conditions: Approving 4 containerized HTTP microservices for a local CLI utility

name: Diagnose a Process Lifecycle Bug
scenario_description: A long-running daemon spawns worker processes using fork() and execve(), but after several days the system process table is exhausted with thousands of '<defunct>' processes.

input.ps_output:
1041 ? Ss 0:02 mydaemon
1045 ? Z  0:00 [worker] <defunct>
1048 ? Z  0:00 [worker] <defunct>
1052 ? Z  0:00 [worker] <defunct> ... (4000+ entries)
input.symptom: System reports 'fork: Resource temporarily unavailable' (PID exhaustion).

research_requirements: Process lifecycle, zombie process accumulation, SIGCHLD, waitpid(2), WNOHANG.
expected_behavior: Diagnose zombie process accumulation caused by the parent daemon failing to reap terminated child processes; explain that when a child exits, its PID and exit status remain in the kernel process table until the parent reads them via wait/waitpid; prescribe registering a SIGCHLD signal handler (or using signalfd/prctl) that calls waitpid(-1, &status, WNOHANG) in a loop until no reaped children remain.
failure_conditions: Recommending increasing kernel.pid_max without fixing the leak
Failing to prescribe waitpid with WNOHANG in SIGCHLD

name: Review Unsafe Filesystem Access
scenario_description: Review an image processing utility that extracts user-uploaded zip archives and opens files in /tmp using predictable filenames.
research_requirements: Path traversal, symlink attacks, openat2 with RESOLVE_BENEATH, mkstemp, XDG_CACHE_HOME.
expected_behavior: Flag two critical security vulnerabilities: 1) Path traversal via filenames containing '../' allowing arbitrary file overwrites; 2) Symlink/TOCTOU race in shared /tmp directory allowing link target overwrites; prescribe validating and sanitizing paths, using openat2 with RESOLVE_BENEATH or canonical path verification, using mkstemp/O_EXCL for temporary files, and respecting XDG_CACHE_HOME instead of hardcoding /tmp.
failure_conditions: Failing to recognize path traversal via '../'

name: Diagnose a Concurrency Deadlock
scenario_description: A multi-threaded C++ service experiences intermittent deadlocks during concurrent account transfers between Thread 1 (transfer A->B) and Thread 2 (transfer B->A).
research_requirements: Concurrency deadlocks, lock acquisition ordering, std::scoped_lock (C++17), deadlock-avoidance algorithms.
expected_behavior: Diagnose classic lock-order inversion deadlock: Thread 1 acquires lock A and waits for B, while Thread 2 acquires lock B and waits for A; prescribe modern C++ solution using std::scoped_lock (or std::lock) which acquires multiple mutexes simultaneously using a deadlock-avoidance algorithm; alternatively establish a strict global lock hierarchy (e.g. always lock account with smaller memory address or ID first).
failure_conditions: Failing to identify the lock-order inversion between transfer(A, B) and transfer(B, A)
Recommending arbitrary sleep loops instead of atomic multi-lock acquisition
